correctness.rationale: For strictly positive continuous histories, quasipositivity and the method of steps preserve positivity; logistic comparison bounds n by finite K. Saturation qH<q/h<=1 bounds p by P, and monotonicity gives strict finite-history bound A=qH(K,P)<1 even at h=q. An explicit exponential supersolution proves global p decay. The reciprocal-prey linear equation with vanishing nonnegative coefficient gives n->kappa. Two-sided scalar DDE comparisons with gains a*±eta prove the exact limit of log p/t, with root uniqueness also for tau=0. For h<q with kappa>1/(q-h), IVT supplies an exact positive equilibrium, sharply refuting a parameter-uniform extension. Algebraic checker confirms displayed rational identities and sample roots; no finite samples are treated as a proof. No assertion of a positive renormalized extinction amplitude.

value.rationale: The motivating paper analyzes extinction risk through equilibrium counts, local stability and numerical bifurcations, while cycle exclusion alone would not provide trajectory convergence. Those do not determine the global fate of all delay histories, nor the quantitative extinction speed. The theorem identifies a sharp and interpretable survival-versus-handling barrier including equality, shows no cooperation-induced rescue regardless of alpha, and supplies a universal, computable exact logarithmic rate at the predator-free state. The coexistence equilibrium construction demonstrates that the barrier is optimal for all-parameter guarantees. This is a structural global dynamical result about a motivated delayed nonlinear system, not a parameter-table recomputation or an arbitrary slice.
